question.text: The Black-Scholes model uses which five key determinants to calculate option price?

answer.text: Underlying price, strike price, volatility, time to expiration, and risk-free interest rate
Underlying price, lot size, tick size, margin, and expiry date
Open interest, volume, volatility, delta, and gamma
Spot price, futures price, storage cost, convenience yield, and carry cost

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, the five Black-Scholes determinants are: (1) underlying price, (2) strike price, (3) volatility, (4) time to expiration, and (5) the short-term risk-free interest rate. The Trap: Lot size, tick size, margin, and expiry date are contract specifications, not pricing inputs. Open interest, volume, and Greeks are market data or outputs. Storage cost, convenience yield, and carry cost are not the five Black-Scholes determinants listed here - the risk-free interest rate is the source-backed funding-rate input. Note: Among the five inputs, only volatility is not directly observable; it is typically estimated or inferred from market prices as implied volatility.
